builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: kw-bench: Breaking Frontier Harnesses on Real-World Tasks
summary: kw-bench replaces rubric- or LLM-judged generative benchmarks with deterministically graded investigative tasks where a correct answer must be recovered from inconsistent real-world evidence. It costs nothing to adopt as an evaluation artifact, but running it requires API access to strong models and multi-hour agent sessions, and the tasks demand filesystem and shell harness infrastructure. What can fail is transfer: results are reported for one task family (SAP VAT reconstruction) and a small set of harness-model pairs, so rankings may not generalize to the reader's domain.
rationale: The paper's actionable finding for a constrained team is that harness choice, not model choice alone, determines capability below the frontier, so the reader should benchmark candidate harnesses on their own investigative workloads before committing to one in production.
technique: Deterministic benchmark for investigative knowledge-work agents

claims.statement: kw-bench replaces rubric- or LLM-judged generative benchmarks with deterministically graded investigative tasks where a correct answer must be recovered from inconsistent real-world evidence. It costs nothing to adopt as an evaluation artifact, but running it requires API access to strong models and multi-hour agent sessions, and the tasks demand filesystem and shell harness infrastructure. What can fail is transfer: results are reported for one task family (SAP VAT reconstruction) and a small set of harness-model pairs, so rankings may not generalize to the reader's domain.

On a five-year VAT reconstruction task with deterministic grading, model-agnostic harnesses scored 0.542 (OpenCode) and 0.528 (micro-cc) on DeepSeek v4.1 Flash while lab harnesses scored 0.00; on Claude Opus 5.5, micro-cc and Claude Code scored 0.9986 and 1.000 in 22 and 25 minutes.
